content.user_title: Build Financial Models and DCF Valuations
content.value_statement: Financial valuation requires consistent assumptions, cash flow projections, and risk testing. This skill provides reusable DCF and sensitivity tools for structured investment analysis.
actual_capabilities: Projects revenue, EBITDA, EBIT, taxes, capital expenditure, working capital changes, and free cash flow.
Calculates WACC from capital structure, market risk, debt cost, and tax assumptions.
Values enterprises with perpetuity growth or exit multiple terminal value methods.
Converts enterprise value into equity value and per-share value.
Runs one-way, two-way, tornado, scenario, and breakeven sensitivity analyses.
Calculates beta from return series and compound annual growth for positive free cash flows.
limitations: The included scripts do not implement the documented Monte Carlo simulation workflow.
The scripts return Python data structures and text, but do not create Excel workbooks or charts.
Default assumptions are illustrative and require validation against current company and market data.
The model simplifies depreciation, capital expenditure, taxes, and working capital relationships.

use_cases.title: Value a Public Company
use_cases.description: Build a DCF from historical results, operating assumptions, market inputs, debt, cash, and share count.

use_cases.title: Test Acquisition Assumptions
use_cases.description: Compare valuation outcomes across discount rates, terminal growth rates, margins, and probability-weighted scenarios.

use_cases.title: Evaluate Project Economics
use_cases.description: Identify breakeven assumptions and rank the variables with the greatest effect on expected project value.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Model Inputs
prompt_templates.prompt: Organize these historical financials and assumptions for a five-year DCF. Identify missing inputs and state every unit clearly.

prompt_templates.title: Build a DCF Valuation
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the included DCF model to project cash flows and estimate enterprise value. Show WACC components and terminal value assumptions.

prompt_templates.title: Test Key Value Drivers
prompt_templates.prompt: Run two-way sensitivity analysis for WACC and terminal growth. Summarize the valuation range and identify unstable assumptions.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Strategic Scenarios
prompt_templates.prompt: Create downside, base, and upside scenarios with probability weights. Add tornado and breakeven analyses for the most important operating variables.

output_examples.input: Value a company with five years of projections, a 9.5% WACC, 3% terminal growth, and $200 million net debt.
output_examples.output: A valuation summary presents projected free cash flow, terminal value, enterprise value, equity value, and the contribution from terminal value.

output_examples.input: Test WACC from 8% to 12% and terminal growth from 2% to 4%.
output_examples.output: A two-way table compares enterprise values for every assumption pair and highlights the resulting valuation range.

output_examples.input: Compare downside, base, and upside cases using probabilities of 25%, 50%, and 25%.
output_examples.output: A scenario table reports each case value, probability, weighted value, and the combined expected value.

best_practices: Document data sources, units, dates, and assumptions before running the model.
Validate WACC, terminal growth, margins, and exit multiples against current market evidence.
Compare DCF results with market multiples and stress tests before making a decision.
anti_patterns: Do not use default assumptions as company-specific forecasts without independent validation.
Do not rely on one terminal value method or one scenario as the final answer.
Do not treat model output as financial advice or a guarantee of future performance.

faq.question: What financial data should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide three to five years of revenue, EBITDA, capital expenditure, working capital, debt, cash, and share data.

faq.question: Which terminal value methods are supported?
faq.answer: The DCF engine supports perpetuity growth and exit multiple methods.

faq.question: Can this skill calculate WACC?
faq.answer: Yes. It calculates WACC from the risk-free rate, beta, market premium, debt cost, capital structure, and tax rate.

faq.question: Does the included code run Monte Carlo simulations?
faq.answer: No. SKILL.md describes Monte Carlo analysis, but the included Python scripts do not implement a simulation function.

faq.question: Can it export an Excel workbook?
faq.answer: No. The included scripts produce arrays, data frames, dictionaries, and text summaries without an Excel export function.

faq.question: Is the valuation suitable for investment decisions?
faq.answer: Use it as an analytical starting point. Validate assumptions, compare other methods, and seek qualified financial advice when appropriate.
